msg: Ultra on root: The tm_dot_prod loop dominates (95.7% of cycles). Each 8-element iteration executes 16 byte loads (5 cycles each), 8 multiplications (5-6 cycles), 7 additions (3 cycles), and loop overhead (~40 cycles/iter). Loads and multiplies are the primary bottlenecks. The custom instruction can fuse packed arithmetic on two 32-bit registers to replace multiple loads, multiplies, and adds per cycle.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product with 32-bit accumulate
proposal.rationale: Replaces 8 loads (40 cycles), 4 muls (20-24 cycles), 3 adds (9 cycles) = ~69-73 cycles with 2 loads (10 cycles) + 1 custom (5-7 cycles) = ~15-17 cycles per 4 elements. 4.3x speedup on the inner loop. Uses 4x 8x8 multipliers + adder tree (~4 DSPs + LUTs).

proposal.title: 2-element int8 dot product with 32-bit accumulate
proposal.rationale: Smaller version of dot4_sum using 2x 8x8 multipliers + 1 adder (~2 DSPs). Replaces 4 loads (20 cycles), 2 muls (10-12 cycles), 1 add (3 cycles) = ~33-35 cycles with 2 loads (10 cycles) + 1 custom (5-7 cycles) = ~15-17 cycles per 2 elements. 2.1x speedup per element. Lower area, composable.

proposal.title: 4 parallel int8 multiplies with pairwise add to 2x16-bit
proposal.rationale: Produces two 16-bit partial sums (p0+p1, p2+p3) packed in one 32-bit word. Replaces 8 loads + 4 muls + 2 adds = ~69 cycles with 2 loads + 1 custom + 1 final add = ~18 cycles per 4 elements. Final horizontal add (add high/low halfwords) done in SW. 3.8x speedup. Uses 4 DSPs + 2 adders.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product with 16-bit saturated accumulate
proposal.rationale: Returns saturated 16-bit result enables wider accumulation in SW without overflow checks. Same compute as dot4_sum but output fits in 16 bits, allowing two partial sums to be packed in one register for later horizontal add. 4 DSPs + adder + saturate logic. ~3.8x speedup on compute, extra SW efficiency.

proposal.title: 2 parallel int8 multiplies with high-halfword add
proposal.rationale: Minimal 2-element dot product returning 16-bit sum (in low halfword). Uses 2 DSPs + 1 adder. Replaces 4 loads + 2 muls + 1 add = ~33 cycles with 2 loads + 1 custom = ~15 cycles per 2 elements. 2.2x speedup. Lowest area, can be issued 4x per 8-element chunk.

proposal.title: 4-element bipolar int8 dot product (1/-1 weights)
proposal.rationale: Specialized for binary/bipolar weights (common in quantized nets). Replaces 8 loads + 4 xnor/popcount + adds with 2 loads + 1 custom. No DSPs needed: 4 xnor + popcount + small adder tree (~LUTs only). 4x speedup on bipolar layers, zero DSP budget.

proposal.title: 8-element int8 dot product (two 32-bit vectors)
proposal.rationale: Processes 8 int8 elements per call (double dot4_sum throughput). The loop processes 32 elements (8 uint32) per iteration; replacing 8 dot4_sum + 8 adds with 4 dot8_sum + 4 adds saves 4*5 + 4*3 = 32 cycles/iter. Over 128 iters/channel * 64 channels = 262k cycles saved. Area: 8x 8x8 multipliers + adder tree ~ 8 DSP + 150 LUTs (~6% budget), fits by sharing DSPs with existing multiplier.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product + 32-bit add (fused accumulate)
proposal.rationale: Fuses the 3-cycle add into the 5-cycle dot4_sum, eliminating 1 instruction per 4 elements. Saves 3 cycles * 8192 calls = 24,576 cycles. Area: same 4 multipliers + adder tree as dot4_sum plus one 32-bit adder (~50 LUTs, 1.5% budget). Requires software to keep running sum in a register and pass it as rs1.

proposal.title: Requantization with baked right-shift (per-channel constant)
proposal.rationale: Replaces 10-12 instructions (mulhi, adds, shifts, clamps) in requant with 1 custom instruction (5-7c). Executed 64 times (per output channel). Saves ~400 cycles. Area: 16x16 multiplier (1 DSP), 32-bit adder, comparators ~200 LUTs (6% budget). Shift amount baked per instruction variant (e.g., requant_s16, requant_s8).

proposal.title: 4 parallel int8xint8 multiplies with pairwise 16-bit add
proposal.rationale: Produces two 16-bit partial sums (p0+p1, p2+p3) in one 32-bit word. Software accumulates these with two 16-bit adds (or one 32-bit add if no overflow) instead of four 32-bit adds. Reduces add pressure and enables wider SIMD accumulation. Area: 4x 8x8 multipliers + two 16-bit adders ~ 4 DSP + 80 LUTs (3% budget). Complements dot4_sum for mixed precision.

proposal.title: 3-element int8 dot product with 32-bit accumulate
proposal.rationale: 512 elements = 170*3 + 2. Replaces 3 dot2.sum calls (15 cycles) + unpacking (9 ALU = 27 cycles) + 2 cross-adds (6 cycles) = ~48 cycles per 3 words with 1 instruction (5-7 cycles). Saves ~40 cycles/iteration. Area: 3x 8x8 multipliers + 2 adders (~3 DSPs + LUTs), fits budget.

proposal.title: Fused requantization: multiply-high, round, shift
proposal.rationale: Requant (1.65% cycles) does 32x32 mulh (5-6 cycles), add round (3), shift (3-5) per channel (64 channels). This instruction fuses all into 1 custom op (5-7 cycles) using 1 DSP for 32x16 mulh + shifter. Saves ~10 cycles * 64 = 640 cycles total. Area: 1 DSP + shifter + adder (~1.5% LUT).

proposal.title: Interleave low bytes of two halfwords
proposal.rationale: Enables cross-word dot2.sum: zip2.lo(w0,w1) packs bytes 0,1 of w0,w1. dot2.sum on zipped registers computes dot2(w0_lo,z0_lo) + dot2(w1_lo,z1_lo) in ONE call. Replaces 2 dot2.sum (10 cycles) + 8 unpack ALUs (24 cycles) + 2 cross-adds (6 cycles) = 40 cycles with 1 zip (5) + 1 dot2.sum (5) = 10 cycles. 4x speedup on low-halve accumulation. Pure wiring (0 DSP, ~0.5% LUT).

proposal.title: Interleave high bytes of two halfwords
proposal.rationale: Complements zip2.lo for high halves (bytes 2,3) of the 32-bit words. Same 4x cycle reduction on high-halve accumulation. Zero DSP, pure LUT wiring. Must be paired with zip2.lo to cover full words.
